about: Starter swaps: parts a person swaps into any toolkit's cart, each a published row (type record:toolkit-swap) whose `swap` is handed in as toolkit_choice.swap, so a way of setting up is chosen apart from the work a toolkit does: any toolkit with any swap is a cart, and no toolkit is written once per way. A pointer is the same { id, door, speaks, label?, credential? } a toolkit's stack holds (read-data/stack-policy.json); a credential is the NAME a person keeps the key under in their vault, never the key. Each part named here is a tool the Workshop ships. The ways of setting up these cover: a site on the person's own domain with their own sign-in, a site with no domain of its own, and the same on a Linux machine the person already runs. An agency runs the own-domain swap once per client, each its own cart; a person on a phone alone takes the toolkit as it stands, whose sign-in already offers passkeys. A company's own sign-in (OIDC or SAML through its identity provider) has no part yet: the official Better Auth tool runs no single sign-on plugin, so no swap offers it.

payload.title: My own domain and my own sign-in
payload.description: A rented computer of your own serves your site and your sign-in, and your own domain points at it.

payload.title: No domain of my own
payload.description: Your site gets a name under a shared address and answers there while your computer is on.

payload.title: A Linux machine I already run
payload.description: The machine you already have is set up over SSH, and every program is built there from its public source.
